lean.name: QuantumComputationSpecs.Algorithms.P450GroundEnergy.Solution.Pi145CompactRouter.r55Branch_twoBody
lean.plain: Signed SELECT on admissible two-body branches
lean.annotation: The two-body branch proof checks a single active row. For each angle bit, the active pair determines whether neither vector, only the first, only the second, or both have that bit set. Both parities equal 1 exactly in the last case. Thus $M_0M_1=M_{01}$ on each one-hot basis word.

lean.plain: Walk blocks at the scheduled workspace widths
lean.annotation: The five inner bits allow 32 addresses. `mainPrepMid_vanish_ge30` gives zero amplitude at 30 and 31, so the block proof uses the SELECT equality on the supported addresses. The zero implementation errors in the walk certificate are relative to the walk with the same prepared weights.

lean.name: QuantumComputationSpecs.Algorithms.P450GroundEnergy.Solution.CompactCore145Bundle.compactCoreTCount
lean.plain: T count of one SELECT core by workspace
lean.annotation: The two rotations nearest the orbital reflection combine into a doubled-angle rotation. At full workspace the other 112 rotations cost 102 T each, the middle rotation costs 98 T, and computing and erasing the one-hot register costs 296 T. The sum is 11,818 T. With $d$ fewer workspace qubits the formula adds $448d+4\max(d-1,0)$ T for $0\le d\le10$.

lean.name: QuantumComputationSpecs.Algorithms.P450GroundEnergy.Solution.Pi145CompactRouter.r55Branch_twoBody
lean.plain: Signed SELECT on admissible two-body branches
lean.annotation: The signed branch assumes `xo'.val < 126`, `b.val < 30` and the prescribed sign `negInPadded`. For $b<29$ the row $58+29r+b$ depends on the orbital vector, while its coefficient depends on the square $(r,c)$. The extra address $b=29$ is a scalar term, so the signed branch applies only the coefficient sign there. The compiled walk handles that sign separately.

lean.name: QuantumComputationSpecs.Algorithms.P450GroundEnergy.Solution.Pi145CompactRouter.r55Branch_twoBody
lean.plain: Signed SELECT on admissible two-body branches
lean.annotation: Expanding Eq. (23) gives $\alpha\beta\oplus\alpha M_0\oplus\beta M_1\oplus M_0M_1\oplus M_{01}$. The controls give $\alpha\beta=0$, and one-hotness cancels the last two terms. The result is zero when the rotation control is off and gives the selected angle bit when it is on. The linked theorem proves the full signed two-body branch equality.
